Men
MEN
n. pl.
Plural of man. Webster 1828: two or more males, individuals of the human race; then males of bravery; then persons, people, mankind in an indefinite sense. The KJV uses the plural for sons of men in their vanity, for nations that are but men, for all men commanded to repent, for the race that needs the one Mediator, and for the charge quit you like men.

Biblical Definition

Men in Scripture is not a branding exercise and not a slur. It is the plural of the creature God made male, and often the name of the race in its need. David rebukes the sons of men who turn glory into shame and love vanity (Ps 4:2). He asks that the nations know themselves to be but men (Ps 9:20) — not gods, not a law to themselves. The gospel then refuses a boutique audience: God now commandeth all men every where to repent (Acts 17:30). Between that race and God there is not a program but a Person: one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus (1 Tim 2:5). The church is not told to dissolve the noun. It is told to inhabit it: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong (1 Cor 16:13). The dictionary therefore keeps two things from collapsing. Male is creational. The Man Christ Jesus is the Mediator of men. Courage in that name is not theater. It is the plural learning again to be what God called it, under the one Man who stands for them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines MEN as the plural of man: two or more males, individuals of the human race; then males of bravery; then persons, people, mankind in an indefinite sense. His bravery line is, We will live in honor, or die like men.

MEN, plural of man. Two or more males, individuals of the human race.

1. Males of bravery. We will live in honor, or die like men.

2. Persons; people; mankind; in an indefinite sense. Men are apt to forget the benefactor, while they riot on the benefit.

Key Scripture

Psalm 4:2 — "O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame? how long will ye love vanity, and seek after leasing? Selah."

Psalm 9:20 — "Put them in fear, O LORD: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah."

Acts 17:30 — "And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:"

1 Timothy 2:5 — "For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;"

1 Corinthians 16:13 — "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong."

Modern Corruption

Men is corrupted when the creational plural is emptied, when quit you like men is recast as either brute swagger or a joke, and when the Mediator is replaced by a process between God and a generic public.

expand to see more

The first corruption is to treat men as a costume. Genesis 1:27 still stands behind the plural: God made them male and female. Late modern talk dissolves the noun into a role you may wear or refuse. Scripture will not. Sons of men in Psalm 4:2 are not a social performance. They are image-bearers in vanity, and they are still men.

The second corruption is to hear 1 Corinthians 16:13 as either a brawl or an embarrassment. The age glamorizes the mocker and then scolds courage as a problem. Paul is not recruiting a mob. He is commanding watchfulness, standing fast in the faith, and strength. Quit you like men is holiness with a spine, not a brand of aggression.

The third corruption is to lose the Man in the middle. First Timothy 2:5 is one God, one Mediator, the man Christ Jesus. Therapeutic religion offers techniques between God and “people.” Political religion offers a cause. The text offers a Man. All men are commanded to repent (Acts 17:30) because that Man is enough for the whole race, and because no other stand-in will do.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Plural of English man. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew ʾîš (H376) at Psalm 4:2; Hebrew ʾĕnôš (H582) at Psalm 9:20; Greek anthrōpos (G444) at Acts 17:30 and 1 Timothy 2:5; Greek andrizomai (G407) at 1 Corinthians 16:13 (quit you like men). No number is added beyond those tags. The companion entry man already treats the singular; this page is the English plural.

expand to see more

Hebrew ʾîš (H376) — man, male, husband (Ps 4:2, sons of men).

Hebrew ʾĕnôš (H582) — man in his frailty (Ps 9:20, but men).

Greek anthrōpos (G444) — man, a human being (Acts 17:30; 1 Tim 2:5, men / the man Christ Jesus).

Greek andrizomai (G407) — to play the man, to act manfully (1 Cor 16:13, quit you like men).

Usage

"Nations must know themselves to be but men (Ps 9:20) — not gods, and not a law to themselves."

"God now commands all men everywhere to repent (Acts 17:30); the audience is the race, not a niche."

"Quit you like men (1 Cor 16:13) is watchfulness and faith with a spine, not a costume and not a brawl."
